messages:
tom: Hi all — joining today. Accepted org invite but when I open private repos I get a banner about SSO + 2FA. I enabled 2FA already. Also my dashboard shows I'm a member of the org but cannot see `redwood-examples`. Any tips?

it-bot: Reminder: Redwood requires SAML SSO + 2FA. If you recently enabled 2FA you may need to re-authorize the org at https://github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/sso and ensure your email is verified.

yana: welcome @tom! quick check: did you accept the invite using your work GH account (tom@redwood) or a personal one? we sometimes see people accept with personal accounts by accident.

tom: i *think* I used my personal GH. I have both accounts and may have clicked the wrong one. How do I fix that without losing my GH profile?

infra: if you accepted with the wrong account the usual flow is: 1) accept invite on the intended work account, 2) org admin removes the personal account member entry, 3) admin adds the work account to the necessary teams. We can help — ping me with the work GH username.

tom: work username is tom-redwood, personal is tom.dev. I just accepted again from tom-redwood but still can't access `redwood-examples` (403).

samir: can you run `gh auth status --show-token` to verify which account gh CLI is using, and `ssh -T git@github.com` to check SSH identity? paste outputs.

tom: `gh auth status` shows:
```
github.com
  ✓ Logged in to github.com as tom.dev (Personal account)
  ✓ Logged in to github.com as tom-redwood (Work account)
  Git operations for github.com: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples (permission: none)
```

tex: interesting — GH CLI shows both sessions but git operations permission is none. That usually means SSO wasn't authorized for the work account or permission sync pending.

yana: did you click "Authorize" for the redwood-inference org when signed in as tom-redwood? also check https://github.com/settings/emails that tom-redwood's work email is verified.

tom: clicked Authorize while signed into tom-redwood and email is verified. `ssh -T` returns `Hi tom-redwood! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.`

infra: i just removed the personal account entry and explicitly added tom-redwood to `onboarding` and `examples` teams. also forced org membership sync. Try signing out of the browser, sign back in to tom-redwood, then `gh auth login` to refresh CLI session.

tom: signed out/in, ran `gh auth login` and then `gh auth status` now shows only tom-redwood active. Trying to open repo page... can see it now. Trying clone: `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/redwood-examples.git` works.

yana: excellent — one extra note for the handbook: if you have multiple GH accounts, use separate browsers or profiles for work vs personal to avoid accidental accept.

samir: and if people hit this again, admins can transfer org membership/force sync. also `gh auth refresh -h github.com` can help in some cases.

tom: thanks everyone! leaving a note in the onboarding doc about using a dedicated browser profile. excited to start the examples walkthrough :tada:
